newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia president to end initial PM talks.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia president to end initial PM talks.

text.p: Slovenian president Milan Kucan will end a first round of party talks aimed at selecting a prime minister for the next government on Tuesday evening, his spokeswoman Spela Furlan said.
Furlan said the president would detail conclusions of the initial talks, which began on Monday, at a news conference at 1300 GMT on Wednesday but analysts said they did not expect an early deal.
Kucan, who must name a candidate by January 3, may hold a second round of talks before settling on a candidate.
"I expect he will name a candidate on the last possible date in the hope of finding a person who could gain majority support in parliament," political analyst Miha Kovac said.

Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, 46, of the centre-left Liberal Democrats is considered the most likely candidate to head the new government. His party is the single strongest parliamentary force and holds 25 of the 90 seats.

The Spring alliance of rightist parties, which controls 45 seats, has thrown its weight behind conservative People's Party head Marjan Podobnik, 35. The centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats are also represented in the alliance.

Parliament must elect a prime minister with an absolute majority within two attempts. If both votes are inconclusive parliament can decide to vote for a third time and reach a simple majority decision.
If all three attempts fail, the president can call early elections.
